# Executive Summary

<!--
This section provides a condensed view of the entire proposal, one page long.
It should be a comprehensive high-level overview that captures the essence of the proposal, including its goals, methods, expected outcomes, deliverables, and budget.
-->


ARcenso is an open-source R package that provides reproducible access to Argentina's official census statistics. The results of the historical censuses are scattered across printed publications, scanned documents, and spreadsheets, and their structures and classifications change from one census round to the next, which makes them hard to access, compare, and reuse. This project will strengthen ARcenso as technical infrastructure for working with these data, and prepare the package for distribution through R-universe and submission to CRAN.

Two complementary lines of work support this goal. The first strengthens the package itself: addressing the quality issues reported by pkgcheck, improving internal data storage and data types, reviewing and adapting the existing functionality, and extending tests and documentation. The second scales how new data is incorporated: a version-controlled pipeline to process and validate historical census tables, combining R-based processing, automated checks, and human review.

With this infrastructure in place, census coverage will be expanded. We will incorporate the 1991 national-level tables first, then progressively add the 1960 census and the subnational tables of the 1980 and 1991 censuses. Along the way we will deliver updated tests, documentation, and reproducible vignettes, together with intermediate releases, leading to a final stable release distributed through R-universe and submitted to CRAN.

The work will run for nine months, from January to September 2027. We request USD 5,500 to support 245 hours of team work, covering package infrastructure, the processing and validation pipeline, the expansion of census coverage, testing, documentation, and distribution. The result will be a more robust and reproducible resource for researchers, public institutions, teachers, students, and anyone else working with Argentina's historical census statistics.
